files_note: Hashes are of the final state of this run. before_after.method: The same inputs are run through `git show bac8282:<path>` of each module and through the working-tree version. The old copy is imported beside its real sibling because both modules resolve REPO_ROOT/DATA_DIR from __file__. BASE_REF is pinned by hash, not to `master`: with a branch name, the first run after this lands would compare the fix against itself, fail, and turn the release gate permanently red.

full_tree_check_redlines.note: Both clean over the same 3071 tracked files, which is the other half of the claim: the stricter check does not redden a healthy tree. The `after` summary line additionally states coverage ('0 file(s) this check could not read'), which the old one could not say. This pair is a DATED MEASUREMENT and is not regenerated by verify.sh: the count it reports includes the two files it is written into, so rerunning always disagrees with the copy on disk by exactly the number of files it just wrote. Regenerate deliberately with `replicate.py --full-tree`; the planted scenarios above are the reproducible check.
